B menolak semua bentuk sejarah lisan kerana buku sudah lengkap.
questions.explanation: Sintesis itu mengekalkan tujuan bersama serta keutamaan berbeza tanpa menukar sokongan B menjadi penolakan.
questions.hint: Pisahkan pendirian umum daripada syarat dan keutamaan setiap pihak.

questions.prompt: Mengapakah B membezakan persetujuan temu bual daripada persetujuan penerbitan?
options: B percaya rakaman tidak boleh difahami oleh sesiapa.
Kesediaan berkongsi dengan penemu bual tidak semestinya merangkumi perkongsian kepada khalayak.
Semua pencerita sudah meminta seluruh rakaman dijual.
questions.explanation: B membezakan dua lingkungan perkongsian berdasarkan kehendak pencerita yang mungkin berbeza.
questions.hint: Bandingkan siapa yang mendengar pada dua peringkat itu.

practice.title: Dua Cadangan untuk Antologi Murid
practice.summary: Gabungkan pendirian tentang pemilihan dan penyuntingan karya.
body: Cadangan A: Antologi sekolah wajar memuatkan pelbagai genre, termasuk puisi, cerpen dan catatan pengalaman. Kepelbagaian itu memberi ruang kepada kekuatan penulis yang berbeza. Pemilihan tidak seharusnya terbatas pada pemenang pertandingan sahaja.

Cadangan B: Saya bersetuju membuka penyertaan dengan luas. Namun, setiap karya yang dipilih perlu melalui penyuntingan bersama penulis sebelum dicetak. Penyunting boleh mencadangkan kejelasan bahasa, tetapi perubahan besar pada maksud patut dibincangkan, bukan dibuat secara senyap. Saya belum memberikan pandangan tentang bilangan halaman antologi.

questions.prompt: Apakah persamaan yang disokong oleh kedua-dua cadangan?
options: Semua karya mesti mempunyai genre yang sama.
Penyunting patut menukar maksud secara senyap.
questions.explanation: A menolak batas kepada pemenang sahaja, dan B menyatakan persetujuan terhadap penyertaan luas.
questions.hint: Cari dasar penyertaan yang sama.

questions.prompt: Pernyataan manakah mengaitkan idea dengan pihak yang betul?
options: A menekankan kepelbagaian genre; B menekankan penyuntingan bersama penulis.
A mahu menutup penyertaan; B hanya membincangkan puisi.
A menetapkan bilangan halaman; B menolak semua penyuntingan.
A mengizinkan perubahan senyap; B mengehadkan penyertaan kepada pemenang.
questions.explanation: A membincangkan keluasan genre dan peserta; B memperincikan proses semakan bersama penulis.
questions.hint: Semak siapa yang menyebut genre dan siapa yang menyebut penyunting.

questions.prompt: Cadangan pelaksanaan manakah memenuhi kedua-dua pandangan?
options: Pilih pemenang sahaja dan cetak tanpa semakan.
Terima pelbagai genre daripada penyertaan luas, kemudian semak karya terpilih bersama penulis.
Buang semua puisi dan ubah maksud tanpa berbincang.
Hentikan antologi kerana dua penulis mempunyai keutamaan berbeza.
questions.explanation: Langkah ini mengekalkan keluasan yang diminta A serta proses penyuntingan yang ditekankan B.
questions.hint: Pastikan langkah pemilihan dan penyuntingan kedua-duanya diliputi.

questions.prompt: Rumusan manakah menambah persetujuan yang tidak dinyatakan?
options: A melihat nilai dalam genre yang pelbagai.
Kedua-duanya bersetuju antologi mesti mempunyai tepat 100 halaman.
B mahu perubahan besar pada maksud dibincangkan.
questions.explanation: Tiada pihak menetapkan 100 halaman, dan B menyatakan bahawa bilangan halaman belum dibincangkannya.
questions.hint: Kenal dakwaan yang tidak mempunyai sokongan dalam mana-mana petikan.

note.title: Read the Gap Between Claims and Behaviour
note.summary: Evaluate a narrator’s self-presentation using precise textual evidence.
body: A first-person narrator offers a viewpoint rather than a complete, neutral account of every event. Compare what the narrator claims with the actions and details the narrative reveals. A contradiction may invite readers to question a particular claim.

For example, a narrator says, “I kept nothing for myself”, then mentions hiding the finest drawing in a desk. That detail challenges the claim of keeping nothing. It does not by itself prove the narrator has lied about every event.
Build an interpretation in stages: identify the claim, select the conflicting detail and explain the narrow inference they support. Consider how wording encourages sympathy or excuses a choice.
Do not replace evidence with a sweeping diagnosis of character. A defensible reading distinguishes an uncertain motive from a contradiction that the text actually establishes.
keyPoints: Compare the narrator’s claims with reported actions.
Explain how a specific detail supports an interpretation.
Limit conclusions to what the contradiction establishes.

reading.title: The Photographs I Chose
reading.summary: Read an original first-person passage about curating family memory.
body: I chose the photographs for the family wall with complete fairness, or so I told my brother. There were only six spaces. Naturally, the picture of me receiving my certificate belonged in the centre. My sister’s photograph showed her repairing our grandmother’s chair, but the background was untidy, so I left it in the envelope. When my brother suggested cropping it, I explained that we had already spent enough time on the arrangement. I found room for a second photograph of my own school ceremony. From the doorway, the wall looked wonderfully balanced. I decided that was what mattered.

questions.prompt: Which detail most strongly challenges the narrator’s claim of complete fairness?
options: The brother stands near an envelope.
The narrator rejects a way to include the sister while finding space for another personal achievement.
questions.explanation: Rejecting cropping while adding a second personal photograph suggests the selection favours the narrator despite the fairness claim.
questions.hint: Compare the treatment of the sister’s picture with the narrator’s second picture.

questions.prompt: What does the final emphasis on “balanced” most plausibly do?
options: It shifts attention to appearance to justify a questionable selection.
It proves that the sister approved every choice.
It establishes the narrator as a professional architect.
It shows the brother destroyed the photographs.
questions.explanation: The narrator praises visual balance after choices that favour personal achievements, offering an appearance-based justification.
questions.hint: Connect the final judgement with the earlier dispute.

practice.title: The Draft Nobody Needed to See
practice.summary: Evaluate a different narrator’s account of writing a speech.
body: “The speech came to me in one clear rush,” I told the club, and they applauded. In my bag lay a notebook filled with crossed-out openings. Leena’s pencilled question beside the fifth draft—“What do you actually want the audience to do?”—had led me to rewrite the ending. I thanked her afterwards for lending me a pen. When she glanced at the notebook, I slipped it beneath the programme. There was no need, I thought, to trouble everyone with the untidy details of inspiration.

questions.prompt: Which evidence most directly contradicts “one clear rush”?
options: The notebook contained multiple revised openings and a fifth draft.
questions.explanation: Several drafts and crossed-out openings show a process of revision, conflicting with the claim of a single clear burst.
questions.hint: Look for concrete traces of the writing process.

questions.prompt: What contribution did Leena make beyond lending a pen?
options: Her question prompted the narrator to rewrite the ending.
questions.explanation: Her pencilled question led to a rewritten ending, which is a substantive contribution to the speech.
questions.hint: Trace what happened because of her written question.

questions.prompt: Which interpretation of hiding the notebook is best supported?
options: The narrator wants to protect the image of effortless, independent inspiration.
The narrator knows the club forbids notebooks.
Leena has ordered the notebook to be destroyed.
The audience has already read every draft aloud.
questions.explanation: The notebook exposes revisions and Leena’s help, so concealing it fits the self-presentation established by the opening claim.
questions.hint: Connect the hidden evidence with the image the narrator presents publicly.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion would be too broad?
options: The narrator has never told the truth about anything in life.
The audience applauded the narrator’s account.
questions.explanation: This passage challenges specific claims about the speech, not every statement the narrator has ever made.
questions.hint: Keep the inference limited to the evidence in this scene.
